item.content:encoded:
In addition to what Zyn said, also keep in mind: Apollyon is an esoteric class. Esoteric classes deviate from the format.

I'm fine with deviating from the format! I've even occasionally done it myself. But Skippy?

He considers a comma splice to be a format screw (one punishable by death). He scorns Daleks for their moderate, bleeding-heart policies. He once erased a man from reality just for suggesting that the Oxford Comma is optional.

You could say he has something of an "opinion" regarding the Apollyon class — and what you can do with it.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I disagree with discouraging esoteric classes and format screws; perhaps for new writers, but overall, no.

Hence the title: "Your Very First SCP!".

Putting aside both Skippy's fanatical (and clearly comical) opposition to format screws and the fact that I myself engage in them, I think discouraging new authors from format screws is a good idea.

Format screws rely on the ubiquity of a format (otherwise, there's nothing to screw!). Every time you stick with the format, you're putting money in the bank; every time you screw the format, you're taking some out. It's fine to cash out — but if no one's putting anything in? It won't be long before checks are bouncing and the electric company is shutting off the power.

Ultimately, there is only one ironclad rule in writing: Write something worth reading. Everything else is window-dressing. But given the youthful demographics of this site (and the tendency for newcomers to want to disrupt the status quo), I think "stay away from format screws" is a good shorthand for "apply format screws sparingly — and only once you understand the format".

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
There's a lot of basic information here that I think a lot of us (who have used the wikidot for a while) take for granted. For example:

Collapsed
– hide block
  • It tells you to bold your headings (and how to bold them; the text demonstrates this directly several times).
  • It tells you to capitalize each first letter in your headings.
  • It mentions to maintain double line-breaks between headings.
  • It introduces the reader to the five standard Object Classes, and provides a simple overview of all five (Safe, Euclid, Keter, Neutralized, Explained).
  • It clarifies how containment procedures should be written as 'are to be' statements, rather than 'should be' or 'will be'.
  • It clarifies the use of metric over imperial.
  • Etc.

Part of the issue is that the people who need this information are less likely to read it in a guide, but I thought maybe if it was tied up in a funny story about a little Clippy knockoff that wants to kill us all it might be faster and easier to digest.

Maybe not, though? This is ultimately an experiment. If I find out this presentation helps newer people understand the basics better, I have ideas for articles in a similar style (explaining how to write an interview log, etc).

ETA: If not, though, I'm just as comfortable letting it be a standalone piece. I want to see how newer readers respond to it.
